thread:
jin: Anyone seeing CI flakes on infra repo? `terraform apply` keeps failing in GHA with an egress / IP association timeout.
sasha: yes, saw 3 fails in a row on `infra-gke` deploy earlier. error was `googleapi: Error 504: Deadline exceeded` when reserving external IP.
mateo: GHA runner logs? is it during `google_compute_address` or when attaching to instances/cloud NAT?
jin: here is the failing snippet from the runner:
```text
Error: Error waiting for Compute Address: operation could not be completed: context deadline exceeded
on modules/network/main.tf line 42, in resource "google_compute_address" "egress_ip":
42: resource "google_compute_address" "egress_ip" {
```
lauren: our cloud NAT / external IP workflow races with node pool creation. if reservation times out then apply aborts and leaves partial state.
ops-bot: [CI] workflow infra/terraform apply #482 failed (job: terraform-apply) <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/482>
jin: notice this is more common in `us-west1-gpu` runners — maybe regional quota or transient control-plane blips. also noticed flaky network egress in recent runner pool updates.
sasha: I also saw leaked addresses after a failed run: 4 ephemeral addresses in the project, cost alarm triggered (~$25/day).
mateo: workaround for now: set `-parallelism=1` for the apply step or bump `timeouts` on `google_compute_address` resource. also add a retry wrapper in the GH Action.
lauren: we should avoid leaving EIPs dangling. propose a cleanup job that runs post-failure to delete unattached addresses older than 10m.
jin: +1. Another idea: create the address resources in a separate plan/apply job that runs before cluster/nodepool ops — avoid the race.
sasha: can we also pin runner regions for infra workflows to `us-central1` where networking is more stable? That reduces flakiness but might increase latency.
mateo: quick triage steps I'm doing now: 1) rerun the failed job with `TF_LOG=DEBUG` 2) check GCP quota & recent control-plane incident 3) run `gcloud compute addresses list --filter="status != IN_USE"` to find leaks.
ops-bot: reminder: terraform state shows 2 addresses in state but only 1 in cloud. Might need `terraform state rm` before cleanup.
jin: I'll open a short PR to split address creation into its own job and add a retry loop around `terraform apply` (3 tries, backoff). assigning to @sasha to run post-failure cleanup playbook.
sasha: on it. I'll also add a small billing note in the PR describing the leak impact and suggested monitoring.
lauren: long-term we should consider using static reserved addresses for critical GPU pools and only create ephemeral for canaries.
mateo: filing an infra incident doc with logs + job ids so SRE can correlate runner preemptions. tagging oncall.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-87 (infra apply network race). See thread in #incidents.
jin: thanks team — will post PR link when ready and schedule a quick sync if failures persist.
